discipline_climbed.desc: Does the climber climb the plan's discipline (a grade range on the plan's scale)?

grades_short.desc: How many grades the plan's easiest grade is above the climber's hardest one (0 when within reach)?

grades_over.desc: How many grades the climber's easiest grade is above the plan's hardest one (0 when not above it)?

distance_known.desc: Is the distance from the climber to the plan known (the plan has a point and the climber a location or area)?

distance_km.desc: How far the plan is from the climber's nearest location or area, in km (0 when unknown)?

group_size.desc: How many people are in the plan's group now, the organizer included? Every one of them must say yes.

open_requests.desc: How many other join requests are waiting on the plan?

days_until_start.desc: How many days until the plan starts (fractional)?

grade_fit.desc: How well the climber's grades suit the plan, 0 to 1. Being below the plan's grades costs more than being above them.
table: Someone who doesn't climb the discipline won't be taken.
The climber's grades overlap the plan's.
One grade short: a group often takes someone close to its grades.
Two grades short: the group may worry about leading or belaying.
Four or more grades short: the plan's routes are out of reach.
One grade above: easy for the climber, still welcome in the group.
Two grades above: may get bored, but safe to climb with.
Three grades above: a mismatch the climber may not want.
Four or more grades above: unlikely to suit either side.

nearness.desc: How close the plan is, 0 to 1: 1 on the doorstep, 0.37 at 50 km; 0.25 when unknown (like about 70 km).

crowding.desc: How much the other waiting requests lower the chance of being taken.
table: Many people are waiting: the group can take only a few.
Several people are waiting: some competition for the spot.
Few or no other requests: no competition worth counting.

timing.desc: Whether there is time for every member to answer before the plan starts.
table: Less than 12 hours: the group may not answer in time.
Within two days: answers have to come quickly.
Enough time for every member to answer.
More than a month away: plans that far out often change.

group_odds.desc: The chance the whole group says yes: each member besides the organizer is one more yes needed.

match_likelihood.desc: How likely the climber asks to join and the whole group says yes, 0 to 1.

table: Unlikely to end in a match.

match_reason.desc: The main reason behind the likelihood, the first that applies.
table: The climber doesn't climb this discipline.
The plan's grades are well above the climber's.
The plan's grades are well below the climber's.
It starts in less than 12 hours.
Five or more people must all say yes.
Ten or more others are waiting on it.
In the climber's grades and within 25 km.
Within a grade or two of the climber's.
